pages.text: It had rained for days. Standing beneath the overhanging roof edge kept you dry; that shelter was called the eaves. Taro stood under the eaves on one side of the road, Mumu on the other. Both looked out into the yards.
"When the rain stops, I'll make something for Mumu." Taro held a blade of grass. Across the road, Mumu held grass, too.
The rain stopped. Mumu came to call Taro. "I'm busy today!" Taro did not come out.
The next day, Taro went to call Mumu. "I'm busy today!" Mumu did not come out.
Taro sat under the porch, carefully weaving three strands of grass.
Mumu sat under the eaves, carefully weaving three strands of grass.
On the third day, they met in the middle of the road. Both hid their hands behind their backs.
Taro held his out first. Mumu held theirs out, too. Grass bracelets! They looked exactly alike.
They put the bracelets on each other's wrists. "You were busy making this!" "You, too!"
Now they wore matching bracelets. Every morning, they waved their wrists in the middle of the road. But the bracelets kept slipping off, so they held on to them as they waved.
